mcqs.q: Bitches with pyometra treated by ovariohysterectomy in a nonspecialized setting had a survival-to-discharge rate of approximately:
mcqs.e: Survival to hospital discharge was 97% (394/405).

mcqs.q: Which findings were associated with greater odds of death after OHE for pyometra?
o: High BUN or a heart murmur
Young age and low body weight
mcqs.e: High BUN concentration or a heart murmur conferred greater odds of death (though predictive power was low).

mcqs.q: What was the study's main clinical message?
o: Pyometra should be referred to specialty centers only
General practitioners can expect similarly high survival outcomes
Outcomes were poor outside referral hospitals
mcqs.e: High survival in a nonspecialized setting means GPs can expect comparable results, widening access to this treatment.

mcqs.q: How did most owners rate their pet's health and quality of life after OHE for pyometra?
o: Better or the same as before pyometra
Unchanged but burdened by chronic disease
mcqs.e: Most owners reported health and QoL were better or the same as before pyometra.

mcqs.q: How did long-term outcomes compare between pets older than 8 years versus 8 years or younger at surgery?
mcqs.e: Reported health and QoL outcomes were similar for pets >8 versus 8 years of age.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about older bitches and queens undergoing OHE for pyometra?
o: Surgery should be avoided in seniors
Without other severe issues they can expect a full life span
mcqs.e: Older animals without other severe health issues can expect to live their full life span.

mcqs.q: Did mild to moderate leukocytosis preclude elective surgery in shelter dogs?
o: No, surgery proceeded safely in all such dogs
mcqs.e: Surgery proceeded successfully for all dogs with leukocytosis.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend regarding preoperative CBC in shelter dogs?
o: Reserve it for ill-appearing dogs, not as a screening test
Perform on every dog before surgery
Use only in adults over 6 months
mcqs.e: A CBC should be reserved for ill-appearing dogs rather than used as a screen, with age-specific reference intervals considered.

mcqs.q: How did leukocyte counts in dogs under 3 months compare with dogs over 6 months?
mcqs.e: Dogs <3 months had higher median leukocyte and lymphocyte counts than dogs >6 months.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Which intervention significantly slowed the rate of rectal temperature decline in cats during OVH anesthesia?
mcqs.e: The active (heated socks) group had a significantly slower rate of temperature decrease than the other groups.

mcqs.q: What was found for plain (unheated) cotton toddler socks?
o: They did not slow the rate of temperature decrease
They were the only effective option
mcqs.e: Cotton toddler socks alone did not slow the rate of temperature decrease versus control.

mcqs.q: What happened to participants' knowledge scores after the 12-day surgical-neutering programme?
mcqs.e: Total knowledge scores rose significantly (mean ~19 to ~28), with gains in all categories.

mcqs.q: How did participants' self-rated confidence in the five common surgical procedures change?
mcqs.e: Self-rated confidence increased for all five procedures after training.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about targeted neutering training for veterinarians?
o: It is ineffective for routine procedures
It can improve knowledge and confidence in canine surgical neutering
mcqs.e: A targeted programme improved knowledge and confidence, offering a way to build surgical expertise for population-management work.

mcqs.q: What was the incidence of stump pyometra after laparoscopic-assisted ovary-sparing spay (LapOSS)?
mcqs.e: No dogs in either group developed stump pyometra during follow-up.

mcqs.q: What must owners be counseled about before ovary-sparing spay?
o: Consequences of retained gonadal hormones and repeated heat cycles
mcqs.e: Owners must be counseled on the consequences of gonadal hormone retention and multiple heat cycles.

mcqs.q: Compared with c-section alone, did concurrent OVH (CSOVH) increase mortality or reduce mothering ability?
mcqs.e: There was no difference in maternal survival, complications, mothering ability, or puppy survival to weaning.

mcqs.q: What differences were seen with CSOVH that the authors deemed clinically insignificant?
o: Longer surgery time and longer delivery-to-nursing time
mcqs.e: CSOVH had longer surgery and delivery-to-nursing times, judged clinically insignificant; CSOVH bitches were perceived as more painful.

mcqs.q: What was the authors' recommendation?
o: Avoid OVH at the time of c-section
Perform OVH concurrently with c-section if indicated, with good pain control
Delay all spays until after weaning
mcqs.e: OVH should be performed with c-section if indicated, emphasizing postoperative analgesia.

mcqs.q: Which agent provided better and longer-lasting postoperative analgesia after major abdominal surgery in dogs?
mcqs.e: Ropivacaine gave lower pain scores than lidocaine and saline and lasted up to 24 hours.

mcqs.q: Which group most often required rescue analgesia?
mcqs.e: Rescue analgesia was needed in 8/10 control dogs versus 1/10 ropivacaine and 5/11 lidocaine.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for major abdominal surgery in dogs?
mcqs.e: Intraperitoneal and incisional ropivacaine was recommended for its superior, longer analgesia.

mcqs.q: Which feline ovarian pedicle ligation method was taught by the vast majority of responding AAVMC schools?
mcqs.e: Double ligation was taught by 34/35 (97.1%) of responding schools.

mcqs.q: Approximately what fraction of responding schools reported teaching autoligation (pedicle tie)?
mcqs.e: Autoligation was taught by 17/35 (48.6%) of respondents.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall conclusion?
o: Significantly fewer schools teach autoligation than double ligation
Most schools have abandoned double ligation
Autoligation is the dominant method taught
mcqs.e: Significantly fewer institutions teach autoligation than double ligation of the feline ovarian pedicle.

mcqs.q: What were the main reasons Turkish veterinarians gave for performing pregnancy termination in dogs?
mcqs.e: The main reasons were 'institutional obligations' and 'demand of the animal owner.'

mcqs.q: What does Turkish veterinary law specify about the timing of pregnancy termination in dogs?
o: Only a first-trimester window is allowed
mcqs.e: No time constraints exist in Turkish law for terminating canine pregnancies.

mcqs.q: The cut-off points veterinarians used for termination ranged across which set of criteria?
o: Possibility of pregnancy, implantation/visibility, heartbeat, and viability
mcqs.e: Cut-offs cited were possibility of pregnancy, implantation/diagnosability/visibility, heartbeat, and viability.

mcqs.q: How was higher reading-grade level (harder readability) of discharge instructions related to outcomes after sterilisation?
mcqs.e: Higher Flesch-Kincaid grade level was associated with greater complication occurrence overall.

mcqs.q: In which species was the readability-complication association significant?
mcqs.e: FRE and FKGL were associated with complications in dogs but not cats.

mcqs.q: What proportion of discharge instructions met the recommended human readability level (grade 6 or below)?
mcqs.e: Only 2% met the recommended readability level; 98% were above grade 6.

mcqs.q: What proportion of private practices reported reluctance to refer pyometra cases to an HQHVSN clinic?
mcqs.e: 80% of private practices would be reluctant to refer to an HQHVSN clinic.

mcqs.q: What did most HQHVSN clinics report about their capacity to treat referred pyometra cases?
o: Most accept referrals same or next day and 95% have needed resources
mcqs.e: Most HQHVSNCs accept referrals same (50%) or next (30%) day, and 95% reported resources to treat most pyometras.

mcqs.q: What was the study's conclusion about partnership between practice types?
o: PP concerns were largely unfounded or fixable, with referral-then-transfer-back opportunities
Pyometra should only be treated at private practices
HQHVSN clinics should stop accepting referrals
mcqs.e: PP concerns were not shared by HQHVSNCs or could be solved by referring for surgery and transferring back for aftercare.
